theory.intro: A prism or pyramid is named after the shape of its **base**.
facts: A **prism** has two identical parallel bases; in a **right prism**, the side faces are rectangles. Name it after the base, e.g. a **triangular prism**.
A **pyramid** has one base and triangular side faces that meet at a point (apex); e.g. a **square pyramid**.
A **cube** is a special square prism; a **cuboid** is a rectangular prism.
Base names: triangle → triangular, square → square, rectangle → rectangular, pentagon → pentagonal, hexagon → hexagonal.
steps: Find the base: prisms have two matching ends, pyramids have one base and an apex.
Name the shape of that base.

workedExamples.question_text: A cube is resting on one of its faces. Give a prism name for the cube and explain why it fits.
workedExamples.solution_text: Two opposite faces are identical parallel squares. These can be its bases, so a cube is a **square prism**.

workedExamples.question_text: A prism has $6$ rectangular side faces. What is its name?
workedExamples.solution_text: Each side of a base meets one rectangular side face. The base therefore has $6$ sides: a hexagon. The solid is a **hexagonal prism**.

workedExamples.question_text: A pyramid has $6$ faces altogether. Determine its name.
workedExamples.solution_text:
One face is the base.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Triangular side faces} &= 6-1 \\ &= 5\end{aligned}$

Each triangular side face meets one side of the base. The base has $5$ sides, so the solid is a **pentagonal pyramid**.

workedExamples.question_text: A prism has $8$ vertices. Determine its name.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The vertices are shared equally between two identical bases.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Vertices on each base} &= 8\div2 \\ &= 4\end{aligned}$

Each base has $4$ sides, so the solid is a **quadrilateral prism**. The vertex count alone does not tell us whether the base is a square or a rectangle.

workedExamples.question_text: A pentagonal prism is resting on a rectangular side face. Does its name change? Explain.
workedExamples.solution_text: Its name stays **pentagonal prism**. Its two identical parallel bases are still pentagons; the face it rests on does not change its name.

foundation.solution_text: The matching bases are triangles, so it is a triangular prism.
Its base is a square and it has an apex, so it is a square pyramid.

foundation.question_text:
A prism has pentagonal bases.
Write its full name.
foundation.solution_text: The base is a pentagon, so the solid is a pentagonal prism.

foundation.question_text:
A pyramid has a hexagonal base.
Write its full name.
foundation.solution_text: The base is a hexagon, so the solid is a hexagonal pyramid.
Its matching bases are rectangles, so it is a rectangular prism.

foundation.question_text:
A pyramid has four triangular faces altogether.
What is its name?
foundation.solution_text: Its base is a triangle, so it is a triangular pyramid.

development.question_text:
A solid has two congruent octagonal ends joined by rectangles.
Name it.
development.solution_text: The matching bases are octagons, so it is an octagonal prism.
Turning it does not change its pentagonal bases, so it is a pentagonal prism.

development.question_text:
A solid has one rectangular base and four triangular faces meeting at an apex.
Name it.
development.solution_text: The base is a rectangle, so it is a rectangular pyramid.

development.question_text:
A cube can be described using a prism name.
Which name and why?
development.solution_text: It is a square prism because it has two identical parallel square bases.

development.question_text:
A prism has $7$ rectangular side faces.
Name the prism.
development.solution_text: Its base must have $7$ sides, so it is a heptagonal prism.

development.question_text:
A pyramid has $5$ triangular side faces.
Name the pyramid.
development.solution_text: Its base must have $5$ sides, so it is a pentagonal pyramid.

mastery.question_text:
A prism has $10$ vertices.
Determine its name.
mastery.solution_text: Each base has half the vertices: $10\div2=5$. The base is a pentagon, so it is a pentagonal prism.

mastery.question_text:
A pyramid has $7$ faces altogether.
Determine its name.
mastery.solution_text: One face is the base, leaving $6$ triangular side faces. The base is a hexagon, so it is a hexagonal pyramid.

mastery.question_text:
A solid is called a triangular prism, although it is resting on a rectangular face.
Explain the name.
mastery.solution_text: Solids are named by their matching bases, not by the face they rest on. Its two matching bases are triangles.
